content_voiceover: This is the master overview slide for autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and the antibody's thermal amplitude is the whole organizing principle. Cold-active antibodies, usually IgM except for paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria which is IgG, increase in activity as temperature drops toward zero degrees Celsius and cause intravascular, complement-mediated hemolysis. Warm-active antibodies, usually IgG, are active at body temperature and cause extravascular hemolysis, predominantly in the spleen. Drug-induced AIHA, classically from methyldopa, is clinically and serologically indistinguishable from idiopathic warm AIHA. The serology table is the high-yield memorization target: cold agglutinin disease is 16 to 32 percent of AIHA, occurs in the elderly, DAT shows C3 only, the antibody is IgM with specificity for the I antigen greater than i greater than Pr. Paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria is about 32 percent of pediatric AIHA, DAT is C3 only, but the antibody is IgG, the Donath-Landsteiner antibody, with anti-P specificity, that IgG-mediated but C3-only DAT pattern is a classic board trap. Warm AIHA is the most common overall at 40 to 70 percent, DAT shows IgG with or without C3, antibody specificity is panagglutinin, rarely anti-Rh. Drug-induced is 12 to 18 percent, with Rh-related, drug-dependent specificity. Clinically, cold agglutinin disease presents with acrocyanosis and livedo reticularis in winter, PCH presents with fever, back or leg pain, and hemoglobinuria after cold exposure, and warm AIHA presents with weakness, dizziness, and hepatosplenomegaly.
keypoints: Cold Ab (usually IgM): active near 0°C, intravascular/complement-mediated hemolysis
Warm Ab (usually IgG): active at 37°C, extravascular hemolysis in spleen
CAD: DAT C3-only, IgM anti-I; PCH: DAT C3-only but IgG Donath-Landsteiner anti-P
Warm AIHA most common (40-70%): DAT IgG±C3, panagglutinin specificity
Drug-induced AIHA (methyldopa) mimics warm AIHA clinically and serologically
keypoint_voiceover: Organize AIHA by thermal amplitude. Cold antibodies are usually IgM, peak activity near zero degrees, and cause intravascular complement-mediated hemolysis, think cold agglutinin disease with acrocyanosis. Warm antibodies are usually IgG, active at body temperature, and cause extravascular hemolysis in the spleen, this is the most common form overall. Know the DAT trap, paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria has an IgG Donath-Landsteiner antibody with anti-P specificity, but the DAT shows only C3, not IgG, because the IgG dissociates at warmer temperatures before testing. Drug-induced AIHA, classically methyldopa, looks just like idiopathic warm AIHA both clinically and serologically.
